summary: PARTIAL is correct. Current code does proposals 1 (16-thread pool), 2 (lazy, async, bounded maintenance probing) and 5 (stall monitor). It also does the static half of 3: the port is bound before the runtime graph, the gate holds requests and serves the static shell and desktop document, and drivers are built only after markHttpServing. So the measured four-driver 3-15 s stall is now off the listener path. Still open: auth/session, RPC and WS wait for the whole RuntimeServicesLive graph, there is no health or status route, and there is no 'upgrading data' state. Migrations and data repairs still run inside the SQLite setup layer before HttpRouter.serve, and four data migrations added since the report (085-088) made that path heavier on large databases. Two corrections to the auditor. First, the 9.5 s and 27 s repairs were one-time; the pr_terminal_at repair is PRAGMA-guarded and will not recur. The recurring exposure is each new full-table migration. Second, proposal 5 is only partly done: the projector replay, the read-model load and the Agent Control listener are not named phases. That is exactly where the unexplained 13 s 'reconcile 863 ms, listen 13170 ms' gap sat.

evidence.note: DESKTOP_BACKEND_UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE = "16". Set at :102 only when the user has not set it; used by main.ts:666 and desktopEntry.ts:108.

The maintenance probe uses resolveCommandPathAsync plus a timed realPath, and runs lazily in a scope fork with a timeout and fallback. The fallback passes resolvedCommandPath: null, so the sync resolveCommandPath at :300 is skipped.
resolveCommandPathAsync has a 1 s bound per PATH entry and skips locations whose earlier check is still stuck.
The registry starts empty and drivers are built only after gateReleased. ProviderService construction (ProviderService.ts:1020-1025) lists only built instances, so it does not release the gate early.
markHttpServing releases the provider boot gate, after HttpRouter.serve has attached.

Build order: StartupStallMonitorLive, then HttpServerLive (the bind), then RuntimeServicesLive, then HttpRouter.serve(makeRoutesLayer) at :807. Every API, auth and WS route still waits for the whole runtime graph.
The gate's early handler serves static assets only (the desktop also gets the document). There is no health, auth/session or startup-status route early, and the codebase has no health route at all.

Held requests get a 503 after 10 s. The client retries 502-504 for at most 15 s (packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:93-95), and the desktop reloads at ready after 9 s (apps/desktop/src/backendAppWindowLoad.ts:30).
runMigrations still runs inside the SQLite setup layer, ahead of the router. It is only wrapped in trackStartupPhase.
The ledger pass and the full post-ledger repair list still run before the router. pr_terminal_at (:282-317) is PRAGMA-guarded and one-time, so its 27 s stall does not recur.

New since the report (60633eff3). CREATE INDEX on (kind, thread_id, sequence, created_at, activity_id) on the largest table. sequence and created_at come after payload_json in the row (005_Projections.ts:49-57 and 008), so building it reads every activity payload's overflow chain, before the router, on a 9 GB DB.
New (36760bffd). length(CAST(payload_json AS BLOB)) scans every payload and rewrites large rows, before the router. It runs once, guarded by a marker.
New (d6a3f6819). A one-time UPDATE of all projection_threads with three correlated subqueries per thread, before the router.

projectionPipeline.bootstrap (projector replay) and getCommandReadModel run during layer build, before the router, and are not trackStartupPhase phases. The same goes for the Agent Control listener start (agentControl/Layers/AgentControlMcpServer.ts:183-199). A stall there is reported with no phase in flight.

recordDesktopStartupPhase is called only for http-bound, http-serving, command-gate-ready and complete (server.ts:296,722; serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1030,1145). trackStartupPhase sends no frames, so the desktop never hears about migration phases. main.ts:3029 only logs them.
Sync resolveCommandPath remains in Cursor probes and session spawns, and in Copilot (CopilotAdapter.types.ts:123). They run after the router serves but block the event loop on a stalled mount.

remaining: 1) Auth/session, RPC and WS still wait for the full RuntimeServicesLive graph (apps/server/src/server.ts:807,830). There is no health or startup-status route, and only static files are served early (server.ts:266-299, httpStartupGate.ts:310-345). 2) Migrations and data repairs run before the router (persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:60, Migrations.ts:663-760), with no 'upgrading data' state anywhere. Since the report, 085 (an index build that reads every activity payload, 085_...ts:42), 087 (a per-thread backfill, 087_...ts:216) and 088 (a payload scan and rewrite, 088_...ts:50-55) joined that path. So the first boot after an upgrade on a large DB can again exceed the 10 s gate hold and the 15 s client retry, and fall back to the desktop's reload at ready. 3) Stall attribution has gaps. Projector replay and read-model load (OrchestrationEngine.ts:601-602), auth and the Agent Control listener start (AgentControlMcpServer.ts:183-199) are not trackStartupPhase phases. Migration phases are never sent to the desktop as frames, because recordDesktopStartupPhase is only called at four milestones. 4) Nobody has measured real-world p90 since the change. 5) Optional: sync resolveCommandPath remains in CursorAgentCommand.ts:49-63 and CopilotAdapter.types.ts:123.
fixDefects: No blocking defects in the implemented parts. The 'proposal 5 done' claim is overstated: the monitor cannot name the layers that held the unexplained 13 s pre-listen gap. Because the window loads at http-bound, a backend slower than 9-10 s fails its first API calls. The client's 15 s auth retry then fails, the desktop reloads at ready, and the user may briefly see an error. That is a known trade-off, not a regression.
implementationSketch: A) Attribution (S, no decision needed). In OrchestrationEngine.ts:601-602, wrap projectionPipeline.bootstrap in trackStartupPhase('orchestration.projection.bootstrap') and getCommandReadModel in trackStartupPhase('orchestration.read-model.load'). Wrap AgentControlMcpServer startListener as 'agent-control.listener.start', and wrap the Auth layer build. Alternatively, add a small helper trackLayerBuild(name, layer) = Layer.unwrap(trackStartupPhase(name, Layer.build...)) and apply it to the big RuntimeServicesLive members in server.ts. Have trackStartupPhase write a desktop 'startup-phase' frame for phases that last more than 1 s, so the desktop log and apps/desktop/scripts/boot-report.mjs capture them. Tests: extend startupStallMonitor tests so a slow fake engine bootstrap shows up in the reported phases. B) Visible upgrading state (S-M, decision). Emit a phase-begin frame from trackStartupPhase for 'persistence.migrations.*'. In main.ts handleBackendFrame, forward it to the window over IPC (preload bridge, not a new HTTP route). The renderer's connection/boot UI then shows 'Upgrading data...' instead of a stalled connect. While a migration phase is running, let the gate extend the hold, or have the client treat 'Ryco is starting' 503s as non-fatal, so long one-time upgrades do not end in an error and a reload. C) Move data backfills off the pre-router path (L, decision). Split runMigrations into a schema pass (DDL, cheap column adds, marker checks) that stays in Sqlite.ts, and a data-upgrade pass (085 index build, 087 backfill, 088 reprojection, the summary backfill). Run the data pass after markHttpServing, gated before signalCommandReady or behind the read paths that depend on it. 087 readers need a fallback to subqueries until its marker is set. 088 is already safe to run late, because readers bound payloads. 085 holds the SQLite write lock for the whole build, so it must finish before the command gate opens. Test with a synthetic multi-GB DB that HttpRouter.serve attaches before the data pass completes and that snapshots stay correct. D) Optional (S): switch CursorAgentCommand.ts:49-63 and CopilotAdapter.types.ts:123 to resolveCommandPathAsync via Effect.promise. E) After a week of use, re-run the boot-log parser on server-child.log to confirm listen p90 and read the 'startup stall' warnings.
decisionReason: Two product and boundary choices. (1) Whether to show an 'upgrading data' state, and whether the gate and client should keep waiting past 10-15 s during known one-time migrations instead of failing and reloading. (2) Whether to defer data backfills behind the router. That means accepting degraded or fallback read paths until the backfill finishes, or reordering the command gate. Serving auth/session or a status route before the auth layer is built would also touch auth semantics. The attribution work (A) and the async Cursor/Copilot resolution (D) need no decision.
correction: The auditor's statement that the 9.5 s and 27 s repair stalls 'still' happen is imprecise. Those repairs are one-time: pr_terminal_at is PRAGMA-guarded and already applied on the user's DB. The recurring risk is each new data migration, and 085/087/088 added since the report put full-table reads back on the pre-router path. 'Proposal 5 done' is also overstated: projector replay, read-model load and the Agent Control listener are not tracked phases, and those are the layers that held the unexplained pre-listen gap. The startup-phase frames the desktop receives cover only four milestones, never migrations.
